title: POC weekly speedcourt - latency & throughput compare vs incumbent (Sprintera)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest lab speed tests comparing Redwood against Sprintera's incumbent provider. Discussed tail-latency spikes, batch sizing tradeoffs, KV/prefix cache effectiveness, and a proposed canary of dedicated slots for high-volume routes. Agreement on three action items: run quantized end-to-end with 2k token traces, provide annotated latency histogram, and schedule a short SLA/billing review with procurement.
action_items: Markus Kruger|Share 1k/2k token representative request traces and golden prompts|2025-08-21
Priya Patel|Run quantized model run (int8-fp16 mix) with prefix cache enabled and upload annotated histograms|2025-08-22
Michael Chen|Send dedicated slot pricing and SLA snapshot + short procurement checklist|2025-08-25
next_steps: Redwood to deliver annotated latency histograms and raw CSV for Sprintera infra team to compare to incumbent numbers
Customer to provide tokenized request traces (1k and 2k distributions) by EOD Thursday
Schedule 30m procurement/finance call for Friday to review pricing and data residency options
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 15:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Attendees: Michael Chen, Priya Patel, Ravi Menon (Redwood) — Lena Ortiz, Markus Kruger, Simone Duval, Ibrahim Noor (Sprintera)

Auto-summary: quick lab readout and triage of tail latency; discuss routing decisions and potential dedicated slot canary; follow-ups on traces and quant runs.

[00:00] Michael Chen: all right folks, thanks for jumping on, uh this is the weekly sprint speedcourt, sorry the weekly poc sync for the Sprintera pilot. quick intros — i'm michael, AE, priya is our se, ravi will help on the cs side.

[00:18] Lena Ortiz: thanks michael, quick note — we had one of our execs watch the previous recording, so they're curious about p99 tail issues we saw last week.

[00:28] Priya Patel: yeah we dug into that — there was a combo of unoptimized batch shaping and a few cold KV cache misses. some of the traces you sent in triggered long kv rehydrates. sorry K V cache rehydrates.

[00:44] Markus Kruger: to be clear, the incumbent had better p99 in our baseline for a small set of very long traces, like 1.5k to 2k. for typical traffic p50/p95 we're fine, but those tails matter for triage and UX.

[01:05] Priya Patel: totally, and that's what we want to isolate. last run we had Redwood hosted with quantize profile A, no prefix caching for that route. we re-ran with prefix cache on and the p99 dropped by about 28% in our lab.

[01:26] Simone Duval: weird — our infra team saw some spikes when the S3-backed KV warmed up. are you folks storing KV in object store or in ram-backed cache for demo?

[01:36] Priya Patel: for the hosted proofs we used the managed prefix cache backed by our in-memory layer, but in the lab harness the test harness pointed to a lightweight object-backed fallback so you might see the warm-up. we should replicate your production-like backend to align.

[01:58] Ibrahim Noor: also, are you doing continuous batching? the incumbent seems to aggregate at 40ms windows and we were testing 20ms windows — that changes throughput.

[02:12] Priya Patel: good point — we have a continuous batching knob, and you can tune the latency SLO vs throughput. we ran three profiles: latency-first, balanced, and throughput-first. the throughput-first bumped tokens/sec by 2.3x but p50 rose slightly.

[02:32] Michael Chen: mike interject — folks, the big takeaway is that at iso-latency p95, Redwood delivered 1.4x throughput vs their incumbent on median traces. but the long traces still have edge cases we need to address.

[02:46] Markus Kruger: can you share the raw csvs? we need to overlay them with our observability.

[02:52] Michael Chen: yes, we'll send annotated histograms and the raw csv from the bench runs. priya will run an int8 hybrid quant and dump the outputs.

[03:06] Lena Ortiz: one concern from compliance — data residency, audit logs. are audit trails full fidelity for inference requests? the procurement team asked.

[03:18] Ravi Menon: we provide audit logs with request IDs, timestamps, route/model version, and redaction controls. we can also show how to integrate with your KMS for key rotation; or for Private deployment we can hand over the control plane.

[03:37] Simone Duval: for PII flows we need SAML SSO + RBAC per team and encryption at rest using our KMS. can you confirm the private deploy meets those?

[03:46] Priya Patel: yes, Redwood Private supports SAML, fine-grained RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. for the hosted pilot we can use customer-managed keys (bring your own key) in most regions — though that requires a short onboarding step.

[04:03] Markus Kruger: great. back to perf — one run last week showed a memory bump where the runtime would pin an extra 2GB for specific models under long contexts, which seemed to cause evictions and increased latency.

[04:19] Priya Patel: that's likely related to kv cache sizing and kernel selection for attention. our runtime sometimes picks a larger kernel for certain sequence lengths — we can force a different kernel selection and also tune kv partitioning to avoid eviction.

[04:34] Markus Kruger: ok can you test forcing the alt kernel and show results?

[04:38] Priya Patel: yes, i'll run that. we'll do: 1) hybrid quant run with prefix cache, 2) alt kernel forced, 3) increased batch cap with smaller aggregation window.

[04:52] Michael Chen: another ask — if we can spin a temporary dedicated slot for two high-volume routes for 24 hours, we can compare isolation benefits vs noisy neighbors in your incumbent. pricing for a 24h dedicated smoke test is simple — i'll send it after.

[05:08] Lena Ortiz: budget is tight but we can carve out a small credit for a 24h smoke. procurement will want the number.

[05:15] Markus Kruger: question — how do you handle fallbacks if a model variant is missing? incumbent does model substitution and sometimes that causes output drift. we need deterministic fallback.

[05:27] Priya Patel: Redwood routing supports fallback chains with compatibility checks (vocab/arch). we log any substitution to the audit trail and we can attach a confidence/metadata field so you can detect drift.

[05:40] Ibrahim Noor: on observability — can your console stream token-level latency per request id? we want to correlate to traces from our APM.

[05:47] Ravi Menon: yes, per-request token timing and per-model kernel metrics are available; retention windows vary by plan but we can export raw traces to your S3 for deeper dives.

[06:03] Markus Kruger: perfect. ok let's walk through the numbers you shared earlier — can you recap the p50/p95/p99 deltas vs incumbent?

[06:12] Priya Patel: sure. in the balanced profile: p50 was 12ms vs incumbent 18ms, p95 85ms vs 120ms, p99 410ms vs 360ms — so p99 was worse in a subset of very long traces. however with prefix cache the p99 dropped to 295ms. with hybrid quant we saw token throughput increase and p95 improved further but p99 sometimes traded off.

[06:46] Markus Kruger: i see — so quant helps throughput but can add variance on tail. is that from dequant steps or numeric underflows?

[06:55] Priya Patel: usually quant introduces small variance during attention and matmuls. we mitigate by mixed precision (keep attention in fp16) and we guard critical paths. that hybrid profile is what we'll run for the next test.

[07:10] Lena Ortiz: is there an easy way for us to reproduce your bench? our infra hates opaque harnesses.

[07:17] Michael Chen: we'll share the bench harness and a small runbook — the harness is a dockerized runner that consumes tokenized traces and emits CSVs and histograms. we'll include the commands to replicate the runs.

[07:28] Simone Duval: make sure the harness uses the same TLS and http keepalive settings as our production ingress. small differences there changed connection setup times in our side-by-side.

[07:37] Priya Patel: noted, we'll match your ingress settings and also include SNI/sample headers.

[07:46] Markus Kruger: another oddity — during high concurrency, some requests hit an internal retry path which increased p99; i suspect retry policy plus small backoff caused that. can you check retry handling on your side?

[07:57] Ravi Menon: yes, we'll include the end-to-end logs. we can also suppress client-side retries in the harness to isolate server-induced retries.

[08:08] Michael Chen: for transparency, we'll attach the Redwood runtime debug level output for the two failing traces — strip PII — but it helps to see kernel selection and memory events.

[08:19] Priya Patel: quick note on routing decisions — you mentioned route A is higher priority. we can create a canary routing policy so high-priority traffic hits dedicated slots and lower-priority hits burst-capacity. that often keeps SLOs intact.

[08:33] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. procurement will want to see both cost of dedicated slots and the unit economics improvements with caching/quantization.

[08:43] Markus Kruger: also, can you provide an example ledger of token accounting per request? we need to reconcile cost across vendor meters.

[08:51] Michael Chen: yes, the console has token-level billing lines per request id; we'll export a sample ledger.

[09:00] Priya Patel: switching gears — security questions. for the private deploy option, are logs encrypted at rest with customer keys?

[09:08] Ravi Menon: yes, for Private we integrate with KMS/HSM and can configure key rotation; we also provide an audit log export that meets SOC2 criteria.

[09:18] Simone Duval: ok good. we might escalate to a security review call next week.

[09:22] Michael Chen: noted, i'll put that on the calendar.

[09:28] Markus Kruger: on the actionables — my team will share traces; what specific format do you want?

[09:33] Priya Patel: tokenized JSONL, with request_id, token_count, and the raw prompt redacted. best if you include distribution of lengths (histogram bucket).

[09:43] Markus Kruger: will do.

[09:46] -- fast forward to 25m mark (lab results discussion) --

[25:00] Priya Patel: ok we ran the hybrid quant with prefix cache enabled and forced kernel B for long contexts. results: p50 10ms, p95 72ms, p99 280ms, throughput +1.9x vs baseline at iso-p95. attached charts will show histograms and boxplots.

[25:22] Lena Ortiz: wow that p99 improvement is meaningful. what about the failure rate or error deltas?

[25:29] Priya Patel: error rates stayed flat ~0.05% — no observable drift in outputs on our automated eval set. there was one mismatch at extreme prompts (very long context >2k) but we flagged it.

[25:44] Markus Kruger: can you mark which runs had object-store backed KV vs in-memory?

[25:50] Priya Patel: yes; the earlier worse p99 run used object-backed fallback in the harness — the improved run used in-memory prefix.

[26:02] Ibrahim Noor: operational ask — when you send CSVs include latency buckets per routing decision so we can map to our ingress.

[26:10] Michael Chen: will do.

[26:16] Lena Ortiz: procurement — just to speed things up, can you give a ballpark for a 24h dedicated smoke?

[26:22] Michael Chen: ballpark i'll email, but rough estimate for the slot we used in lab is $X per 24h — i'll detail in the deck.

[26:31] Simone Duval: another note — we want export of audit logs to our S3 with 90d retention initially. possible?

[26:38] Ravi Menon: yes, export possible and retention configurable. we'll include the steps for S3 export config.

[26:45] -- last 15 minutes: triage and wrap up --

[33:10] Priya Patel: so short recap of technical next steps: 1) run quantized hybrid with prefix in-memory cache (priya), 2) force alt kernel for long contexts (priya), 3) provide raw CSV/histograms and runtime debug snippets (michael/ravi), 4) customer sends traces (markus).

[33:40] Markus Kruger: agreed. also we want a short failback playbook doc showing routing fallback chains and detection thresholds.

[33:48] Michael Chen: we'll add that to the artifacts.

[34:02] Lena Ortiz: scheduling — can we do procurement sync on Friday 09:00 PDT?

[34:08] Michael Chen: i'll propose 09:00 and include cost snapshot.

[34:12] Simone Duval: last question — if we do a 24h dedicated canary, any SLA difference?

[34:19] Ravi Menon: dedicated slots have a tighter SLA and more predictable latency; for a short canary we can apply a temporary SLA note in writing for the duration.

[34:29] Markus Kruger: ok. thanks everyone.

[34:33] Michael Chen: thanks all — i'll circulate the artifacts and the bench harness, priya will run the quant runs and post results. recap in the calendar invite. next sync same time next week unless we escalate to security call sooner.

[34:46] Lena Ortiz: thanks, bye.

[34:48] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains minor ASR errors (eg Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated, K V spelled out). references to external artifacts: bench-harness repo link (shared after call), pricing snapshot (to be sent), annotated histograms (to be uploaded).
questions: Can we get dedicated slot pricing for 24h smoke?
What's the exact format for tokenized traces?
